standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the centrality equation eta = kappa I into the identity (-lambda)^ell = kappa^2, which forces ell to be even.

core_obligations: Take a word eta = eta_1 ... eta_n alternating the generator s with the generators p, p^{-1}, and let ell be the number of occurrences of s; rule out ell = 0 by noting that p and p^{-1} are not central (proof lines 841-857).

Read the word as a polynomial f in lambda with matrix coefficients of degree at most ell, and prove the degree is exactly ell by computing the coefficient m of lambda^ell: it is obtained by replacing each s with s_1, and using s_1 p s_1 = -s_1 and s_1 p^{-1} s_1 = s_1 gives m in {+- p^i s_1 p^j}, which is nonzero (proof lines 858-896).

Use centrality: if eta is central then eta = kappa I; taking determinants in eta_1...eta_n = kappa I and invoking the cited determinant formula yields (-lambda)^ell = kappa^2, so ell is even and kappa = +- lambda^{ell/2} (proof lines 897-905).

Conclude the contradiction: the polynomial f would then have degree ell/2, which is strictly smaller than ell, contradicting the claim that its degree is ell; hence no such central eta exists and the action is faithful (proof lines 906-910).
proof_roadmap: Assume a central word and organise it as an alternating word in s and p^{+-1}, quantifying the number ell of s entries (proof lines 841-857).
Pin the top coefficient of the resulting matrix polynomial, then use centrality and the determinant formula to force a smaller degree, a contradiction (proof lines 858-910).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the action of PSL_2(Z) on the algebra Lambda is faithful (statement lines 834-838). The proof argues by contradiction on a central word: after writing the word in the alternating form eta_1...eta_n and letting ell be the number of occurrences of s, it reads the word as a polynomial in lambda with 2x2 matrix coefficients, shows the top coefficient is nonzero by the two relations s_1 p s_1 = -s_1 and s_1 p^{-1} s_1 = s_1, and then compares degrees: centrality forces eta = kappa I, determinants force ell even and kappa = +- lambda^{ell/2}, so the polynomial would have degree ell/2 rather than ell (proof lines 841-910). The decisive step is the degree comparison, which needs both the explicit top coefficient and the determinant identity; both are computed inside the span. H2.
